reasons: No tests are visible in the packet to confirm validation behaviour.
Field meanings are not documented beyond names.

terms.meaning: A label stating which layout of the record is being used, so later changes can be tracked.
A catch-all area for source-specific data that does not have its own field.
A Python library that checks that data has the expected types and fields.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and version number
sections.what: Brings in the date and validation tools and sets the schema version to 1.0 for every record.
sections.why: The version number lets future changes to the record layout be recognised.

sections.name: NormalizedActivity
sections.title: Activity record layout
sections.what: Describes one schedule task: its identifiers, name, work breakdown location, planned, actual, baseline and forecast dates, status and task type. Unknown fields are rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed shape for tasks lets the rest of the app compare schedules from different sources.
sections.watch_out: Each date field is optional, so code using them must handle empty values.

sections.name: NormalizedRelationship
sections.title: Relationship record layout
sections.what: Describes one link between two tasks, including which project each task belongs to, the relation type and the lag in hours.
sections.why: Keeping links in their own record lets the app check dependencies without reading the tasks again.
sections.watch_out: Lag is stored in hours, so a source that uses days must be converted before it reaches this record.

sections.name: NormalizedProject
sections.title: Whole project summary layout
sections.what: Describes one project: its name, dates and counts of activities, relationships, work breakdown items, calendars, resources, codes and user-defined fields, plus flags for whether actuals, baseline or forecast data exist.
sections.why: The counts let the app show a project overview without loading every task.
sections.watch_out: Every count and flag is required, so the code that builds the summary must always supply them.

summary: Defines the strict shape of normalized schedule records for activities, relationships and whole projects.
purpose: Sets a fixed, checked format so that any schedule source ends up with the same fields before the rest of the app uses it.
why: Likely reason: source-neutral records let the app treat different scheduling tools the same way. Strict checking catches bad data early.
how: Defines three record types. Each one has a schema version, identifying fields, optional dates and status text, a free-form extensions dictionary, and a source row number. Each record rejects any field it does not declare.
inputs: Values from the service module that reads the staging database, or any other code that builds these records.
outputs: Validated record objects, or validation errors when a value has the wrong type or an unknown field is present.
risks: Adding a field to a record requires changing both the record definition and the code that fills it, or validation will fail.
debug: When a record is rejected, read the error for the field name. Check whether a newer source added a field that is not declared here.
